text:
After closing, kennel cleaning stood out in your complaint, and we are sorry that the post-flight condition of the animal area did not meet the standard you should expect from Aurelia Skyways. You reported that the crate environment felt neglected and that the handling around your pet was not as orderly as it should have been. We reviewed the desk record and the service notes tied to the trip, and we have treated this as a process issue rather than an isolated remark.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk expects prompt, respectful communication at every stage, and we want each traveler to see that standard in the way we handle animals and follow through on service changes. Every animal receives patient attention from trained staff, and the cleaning and handoff steps are meant to be consistent from check-in to release. When a kennel is left in a poor state, it points to a breakdown in routine work, and that is something we need to correct without delay. We have already passed the report to the operations lead so the cleaning sequence, supply check, and final inspection flow can be reviewed against current practice.

We also understand how stressful it is when a pet has already been through travel and the return handoff does not feel calm or well managed. That is not the experience we aim to deliver. Our desk ledger is used to record service changes and follow-up notes so that staff can track where a process slipped and what needs to be reinforced. In this case, the note will support a review of kennel cleaning, transfer oversight, and the final visual check performed before release. The objective is straightforward: cleaner equipment, clearer ownership, and a better handoff for the next traveler and pet.

We regret the trouble this caused and appreciate that you took the time to raise it. Aurelia Skyways will use this report to tighten routine work and protect the welfare of animals in our care. Companion Animal Travel Desk
